issues: Global compile blocker: the timeline supplies only broad fractional windows, not exact native-frame events for releases, catches, contacts, hinge seats, roof landings, water impacts, state changes, or carriage stops. Without event frames, the required six-frame pre/post evidence windows and ordered cause-before-result checks cannot be generated reliably.

Focus registration is incomplete. Compound focal IDs such as `aligned-roof-profile-pair`, `leak-droplet-and-floor-contact`, `paper-gold-rollback-carriage`, and `restored-rowhouse-and-seated-history-spine` are listed as parts but are conceptually groups. Each needs an explicit registered focus-group mapping to real geometry and bounds; declaring an ID alone must not create a selector.

Shot 01 has unresolved handoffs. Bot grips the teal roof, yet the roof subsequently falls; no release event is specified. Bot also arrests the coral roof without a declared coral-roof contact or grip anchor. Define the release, the replacement arrest mechanism, and their exact event frames.

Shot 02 lacks a visible initiating cause for the catch tongue and accordion deployment. Make the falling roof trip a registered latch or carry forward a visibly driven mechanism from shot 01. A self-starting rescue weakens cause-effect.

Shot 03's checkpoint relief appears as the plate passes behind the house, but no pressure, scan, keyed contact, or finite state adapter explains the imprint. Register a physical capture mechanism and the affected features rather than relying on an unexplained reveal.

Shot 04 asks an absent Bot to lift the teal roof, install the coral roof, open the folio, and align the comparison without a visible actuator. It also compresses four consequential stages into 50 frames. Add a registered mechanical driver and simplify or lengthen the sequence so the changed roof geometry remains readable at mobile size.

Shot 05 requires production-specific adapters for the progressive teal wet-state reveal, asymmetric floor sag, pooled-droplet compression, and window contact. These are not established merely by registering part names. Define finite states, masks or permitted transforms, plus exact impact events; otherwise the instructions may be silently ignored.

Shot 06 declares two Bot hands on separate checkpoint-tab grips, but only one tab part and no left/right grip anchors are registered. The inverse-grip contract must name two real anchors and solve them after both carriage and reaction transforms.

The rollback does not conserve the failed floor state. Shot 06 flips the same floor to hide its wet face, while shot 08 later displays a separate wet-test history leaf that was never transferred or captured. Archive the actual wet floor component into the failed-state bay while installing the checkpointed dry floor; do not create the failed evidence later.

Shots 07 and 08 again use autonomous motion—the rain ribbon descends, the history spine unfolds, and the return tab reverses—without an operator, stored-spring release, or registered drive mechanism. Expose a repeat-test actuator and a return-drive cause before their results.

Reactions applied to actively articulated composites, especially `paper-gold-history-strip` and the moving rollback roofs, need explicit transform composition order and segment ownership. A whole-strip reaction cannot conflict with its authored hinge transforms, and held parts require grip resolution after both transforms.

Shot 08's three-state fan, live house, archive rail, cup, droplets, and caption-safe boundary create a credible mobile-density risk. Specify which state silhouettes remain fully readable at 360×640 and which details may be suppressed during the fan.

The asset ledger identifies the reused and production-specific assets with paths, metadata paths, and the agent-assisted addition, but `candidate-reusable` and `canonical-promoted` exist only as a prose absence in `asset_promotion`. If the planning schema requires all four scopes, record those two scopes explicitly as empty/not promoted.
